general.title: Group and timebox your work in Cycles.
general.description: Break work down by timeboxed chunks, work backwards from your project deadline to set dates, and make tangible progress as a team.

comic.title: Cycles are repetitive time-boxes.
comic.description: A sprint, an iteration, and or any other term you use for weekly or fortnightly tracking of work is a cycle.

no_issues.title: Create a work item and assign it to someone, even yourself
no_issues.description: Think of work items as jobs, tasks, work, or JTBD. Which we like. A work item and its sub-work items are usually time-based actionables assigned to members of your team. Your team creates, assigns, and completes work items to move your project towards its goal.

comic.title: Work items are building blocks in pbot.
comic.description: Redesign the pbot UI, Rebrand the company, or Launch the new fuel injection system are examples of work items that likely have sub-work items.

general.title: Map your project milestones to Modules and track aggregated work easily.
general.description: A group of work items that belong to a logical, hierarchical parent form a module. Think of them as a way to track work by project milestones. They have their own periods and deadlines as well as analytics to help you see how close or far you are from a milestone.

comic.title: Modules help group work by hierarchy.
comic.description: A cart module, a chassis module, and a warehouse module are all good example of this grouping.

general.title: Write a note, a doc, or a full knowledge base. Get Galileo, pbot's AI assistant, to help you get started
general.description: Pages are thoughts potting space in pbot. Take down meeting notes, format them easily, embed work items, lay them out using a library of components, and keep them all in your project's context. To make short work of any doc, invoke Galileo, pbot's AI, with a shortcut or the click of a button.
